justice: The complete absence of paved sidewalks forces pedestrians, including elderly and child users, to share the main roadway, reflecting poor spatial equity.
The lack of tactile paving and designated safe paths creates severe fairness issues for visually impaired road users.
Unpaved, muddy shoulders and right-of-way encroachment by stacked wooden pallets eliminate accessibility for wheelchair users and those with mobility aids.
safety: The lack of separated pedestrian or bicycle lanes forces mixed traffic on a narrow paved surface, significantly increasing collision risks.
Massive stacks of wooden pallets on the right side encroach on the road edge, creating dangerous blind spots and narrowing the passable area.
A visibly leaning utility pole and a chaotic web of overhead wires present structural hazards to passing pedestrians and vehicles.
livability: The encroachment of industrial storage materials (wooden pallets) into the street space degrades the community living environment.
The complete absence of public seating or resting facilities makes the street inhospitable for elderly residents needing breaks.
The combination of hanging laundry on trees and unkempt dirt shoulders reflects a lack of organized, usable public space.
sustainability: The absence of dedicated active transportation infrastructure, such as bike lanes or transit stops, fails to encourage low-carbon travel.
Unpaved, rutted dirt edges along the roadway indicate poor stormwater management and a lack of proper green infrastructure.
While a few trees exist on the left side, the street heavily prioritizes motorized vehicle access over ecological integration.
aesthetics: Large, disorganized stacks of wooden pallets dominate the right side of the visual landscape, creating a cluttered and industrial appearance.
Dense, unstructured overhead power lines and a leaning wooden pole disrupt visual harmony and sky views.
The juxtaposition of informal laundry lines, muddy shoulders, and industrial debris results in a highly disjointed and unkempt streetscape.
comfort: The lack of street-lining canopy trees directly over the paved roadway provides zero thermal comfort or shade for pedestrians in hot weather.
The complete absence of street furniture like benches drastically reduces physical comfort, particularly for elderly individuals.
Muddy, uneven road shoulders force pedestrians to walk on the hard asphalt next to vehicles, increasing psychological stress and physical discomfort.
walkability: The total lack of paved sidewalks forces pedestrians to walk directly in the vehicle lane, severely compromising walking safety.
Muddy terrain on the left and stacked wooden pallets on the right eliminate any viable off-road walking paths.
The absence of crosswalks, dedicated pedestrian space, and traffic calming measures makes navigating the street highly stressful for vulnerable groups.
bikeability: The absence of dedicated or protected bike lanes forces cyclists to share a narrow, unmarked road with motor vehicles.
A parked truck and protruding wooden pallets on the right side create dangerous pinch points that endanger passing cyclists.
The lack of clear lane markings or signage reduces the predictability of traffic flows, lowering overall cycling feasibility.
